epic.title: compat(native): dialog, shell, Menu/Tray, clipboard, screen, nativeTheme, nativeImage, Notification, safeStorage and power/shortcut brokers behind generated grants
epic.body:
## Scope
38 entities / 350 members, all main-process: Menu (13), MenuItem (21), Tray (36), dialog (8), Notification (30), clipboard/ClipboardItem (11), shell (7), screen/Display (31), globalShortcut (7), powerMonitor (16), powerSaveBlocker (3), nativeTheme (9), nativeImage/NativeImage (24), systemPreferences (28), safeStorage (8), pushNotifications/inAppPurchase (mac), desktopCapturer (Tier 3), ShareMenu. Live today: keld-native ships only the retained FsBroker (fs.read/fs.write) and a MODULES name list (`capture` is missing from it: code/spec gap); no F06 channel is reachable until KEL-102/T3 admission; `@keld/electron` exports only `app`.

## Corpus demand
dialog (draw.io showMessageBox ×7 incl. one `showMessageBoxSync` on the close path, open/save ×4 each; Zettlr showMessageBox 24, dialog in 21 files) > shell (openExternal, openPath, showItemInFolder, trashItem) > Menu (both: buildFromTemplate + setApplicationMenu; 13 roles in draw.io; 45 accelerators per Zettlr platform menu; popup) > screen > clipboard (draw.io uses the W3C promise shape with ClipboardItem; Zettlr sync readText) > nativeTheme (themeSource, `updated`) > nativeImage (createFromDataURL().toPNG(), createFromPath) > Tray/Notification (Zettlr) > systemPreferences (accent colour, theme-changed notification). Zero use of globalShortcut, powerMonitor, powerSaveBlocker, safeStorage, pushNotifications, inAppPurchase, ShareMenu, desktopCapturer.

## Maturity ladder
- L0: every module exists; unsupported members throw typed errors; `capture` added to MODULES or named as intentionally absent.
- L1: dialog/shell/Menu/screen/clipboard/nativeTheme/nativeImage work for draw.io and Zettlr on macOS through guarded brokers.
- L2: dialog-minted scopes, menu role execution host-side, accelerator semantics, theme `updated` event, clipboard shapes pass pinned entries on each OS.
- L3: corpus workflows pass under `keld dev` with KEL-74 records and `app.system` grants recorded.

## Linear owners consumed
KEL-130 (FsBroker retained scopes — dialog grants extend the same set), KEL-102 (broker admission; the guard's accepted operation set is hard-coded to fs.read/fs.write today), KEL-89 (secrets/auth), KEL-78 (strict: no keychain reach from the child), KEL-132, KEL-208/KEL-209 (URL-scope authority rule), KEL-19/KEL-103 (Windows AppUserModelId, bundle metadata).

## Design facts from research (NOT yet independently refuted — batch 2 refutes; decisions below stay open)
- Host-owned UI handles: every Menu/MenuItem/Tray/Notification/popup is a host main-thread resource with a host-assigned `(generation, id)`; facade proxies are write-through; clicks arrive as host→Bun messages; `role` items execute host-side without a round trip (Electron ignores `click` when `role` is set).
- Resource-less capabilities keep the arch 03 §2 literal shape `app.system: ["clipboard.read", …]` evaluated with the existing matcher (operation=system, path=literal) — no guard schema change.
- NativeImage is a Bun-side immutable value object (bytes + sniffed format + size + representations); decode/encode happens host-side only at consumption; clipboard baseline is the v44.4.5 W3C shape.
- safeStorage is a thin facade over a host `secrets` module; Linux `basic_text` plaintext degradation is reported, never emulated.
- Blocking dialogs (`showMessageBoxSync`, draw.io close path) depend on the panel's S0 link-drain gate; until then they are SCAFFOLDED (typed throw + fix-it) or served through the worker-owned transport once approved.

decision_tickets.title: Dialog-minted filesystem scopes: generation-bound session grants in the FsBroker retained set (sibling pattern for draw.io .bkp) — approve the permission-model shape
decision_tickets.question: Proposed (unrefuted): the host dialog returns paths and registers each as a generation-bound fs scope into KEL-130's retained set (open → read leaf, save → write leaf + declared sibling pattern), revoked on generation death, never persisted. Needs an independent refutation (batch 2) and a permission-model review; the user-granted-roots-survive-restart question is a separate KEL-79/KEL-130 spec gap.

decision_tickets.title: Resource-less capability grants (clipboard, notifications, tray, shortcuts, power): keep `app.system` literals evaluated with the existing matcher?
decision_tickets.question: Proposed (unrefuted): evaluate `app.system` literals as operation=system, path=literal with the existing matcher — zero guard schema change. The guard's accepted operation set is hard-coded to fs.read/fs.write today, so admission for new operations is a KEL-102 change; confirm with the owner.

decision_tickets.title: shell.openExternal confirm-per-scheme grant (`confirm:https`) vs exact literals only — permission-model decision (joint with X04-D4)
decision_tickets.question: Median apps open arbitrary https/mailto/tel links; scheme-wide globs are inert by the KEL-208 authority rule. Proposed: a confirm-class grant (host-rendered confirmation showing the full URL) alongside literal scopes; `file:`/`javascript:` never. Needs KEL-208 owner ruling on spelling; the broker must canonicalise before matching.

invariant_violations.violation: Title and build text commit to a 'confirm-per-scheme grant' while the governing permission-model decision (X04-D4) is open and F06-EPIC's never list contains 'scheme-wide shell.open globs'. A confirm-class token is a scheme-wide allow mediated by a click — a new authorization source for generated default-deny that needs an approved spec before it appears as a build instruction.

invariant_violations.violation: Runtime-minted grants: dialog-chosen paths 'registered as generation-bound retained scopes' add a grant source outside the generated manifest (unique #4: generated, host-enforced default-deny). The ticket embeds the unapproved shape (F06-D1 is 'proposed (unrefuted)') as its build and AC.

invariant_violations.violation: 'Entries may fail (red) until the implementing tickets land; they must not be skipped or retried' collides with the verification floor (reported passing workspace tests; merge admission enforced — KEL-128 Done) and with 'MUST NOT weaken tests / skip gates'. No mechanism is named that lets a red entry coexist with a green required gate.
invariant_violations.fix: State the mechanism as a contract: entries are KEL-74 cells recorded with an explicit expected status (fail/unknown) asserted by the runner, flipped to pass in the implementing PR; a silently red or ignored test is not allowed.

invariant_violations.violation: Features without a spec: labelled ready-for-agent 'task' with Review gates none/permission-model, yet they add implementation — net.fetch event-ordering facade and a new keld-native net row (F05-T6); Notification broker + secrets module + typed facades for eleven modules (F06-T6); app.getAppMetrics as a new host Call (F08-T2). Also 'one concern per PR'.
invariant_violations.fix: Reduce each to publishing scoreboard rows; any broker/Call/facade becomes its own needs-spec ticket when a corpus call site demands it.

invariant_violations.violation: Doctrine §11/§14: marked ready-for-agent although their epics state the research is 'NOT yet independently refuted — batch 2' (swarm.json holds 0 refuter verdicts for F06, X03, X05).
invariant_violations.fix: Hold at needs-triage until the batch-2 verdicts are applied; then relabel.

quality_problems.problem: AC1 'draw.io close dance ... completes without data loss and without timeouts' is not binary (no observable for data loss; 'without timeouts' bans a mechanism) and, for a modified document, is unsatisfiable while F06-T2 AC4 makes showMessageBoxSync throw. Negative control 'host auto-closing on a timeout fails the data-loss test' needs a time source — unspecified, and sleeps are banned.
quality_problems.fix: Two ACs: (a) unmodified document: close → isModified → destroy → exactly one `closed`; (b) modified document: prompt shown, Save path writes the file then destroys — explicitly gated on the PANEL-P1 outcome. Negative control: inject the host timer through a controllable clock.

quality_problems.problem: Disjunctive ACs that cannot fail: 'either implemented or a typed ▲' (F02-T5 AC2), 'either pass the same entries or carry an explicit per-engine ▲' (F03-T2 AC4), '✔ or ▲' (F04-T4 AC4), 'round-trips once the broker lands; until then the typed error' (F06-T6 AC2).

ambiguity_laundering.claim: AC1 'draw.io open → edit → save completes through the broker with no manifest widening'; AC2 'a sibling outside the declared pattern is denied'.
ambiguity_laundering.problem: draw.io's main process reads and writes files with node:fs (imports at electron.js:1-2; saveFile/readFile actions at :4441-4493). verdicts.reason: The direction (host-minted dynamic grants flowing into the FsBroker scope set; arch 05 dialog row 'scoped-path grants flow into fs scopes') stands, and the Electron return shapes are correct. But the specific mint shape is contradicted by the very drawio oracle the decision cites, on four points. (1) 'open -> fs.read leaf' is wrong: drawio blesses every open-dialog path and its write gate accepts any blessed path, so File>Open then Save writes back to the opened path with no save dialog. A read-only open grant fails F06-T2's own acceptance criterion 'draw.io open -> edit -> save completes'. (2) The sibling pattern '<name>.*' matches none of drawio's siblings: they are prefix-named ('.$' + basename + optional counter + '.dtmp', '.$' + basename + '.bkp', legacy '~$' prefix) and matched by startsWith. The trap's test oracle 'write <path>.bkp' is therefore also wrong. (3) 'revoked on generation death and never persisted' breaks Open Recent: drawio persists its blessed set (cap 500) in electron-store specifically so Open Recent works across launches, and it also blesses paths that never came from a dialog (argv, second-instance, macOS open-file). (4) Leaf grants do not cover Zettlr's directory picks (openDirectory + createDirectory), which need subtree read+write and are persisted as workspace roots. Sequencing: the first proof runs drawio under the explicit legacy profile (ambient fs), so D1 is not on the first-proof path and should be parked as a decision ticket, not designed in detail now.

verdicts.reason: Host ownership of UI handles, host-to-Bun click dispatch with (commandId, focused window, KeyboardEvent), one shared accelerator parser, and host-side role execution all match Electron's own structure: one StringToAccelerator used by menu and globalShortcut; on macOS role items are wired to native selectors; click receives (event, focusedWindow, focusedWebContents). The doc quotes are exact. Four corrections do not overturn it. (1) The 'unknown' popup ordering is determinable from source for macOS: menu-will-close fires first, then the item click, then the popup callback (the close callback is deliberately posted async 'so that itemSelected runs before the close callback'). Zettlr's comment says the same. The F06 trap oracle 'click then will-close then callback' is wrong. (2) 'Electron ignores click when role is set' is the doc sentence, but the implementation falls back to the user click when role execution returns false (macOS-native roles in JS, or a window/webContents role with nothing focused), and quit/close roles run app.quit()/window.close(), which emit vetoable events - so 'without a round trip' is false for those two. (3) Item properties (checked, enabled, label, menu.items) are synchronous getters and the checkbox flip happens in JS on click, so Bun must hold the authoritative item state with the host as projection; the rejected alternative (a) 'two sources of truth' is partly unavoidable and the ticket should say which side is authoritative. (4) The default menu is a JS Menu built from five role items at will-finish-launching and is visible through Menu.getApplicationMenu(); building it 'host-side' only would make getApplicationMenu() return null where Electron returns a Menu - build it in the facade through the normal setApplicationMenu path and delete the special case. Sizing: first-proof demand is the application menu only (drawio: buildFromTemplate + setApplicationMenu with role items and a few click items; setApplicationMenu(null) off-mac). Tray, Notification and popup have Zettlr-only demand (one site each family); globalShortcut and powerSaveBlocker have zero resolved call sites. Split D2 so only the application-menu slice is on the first-proof path.

verdicts.reason: What survives: the v44.4.5 W3C clipboard shape as baseline (drawio's one clipboard path uses exactly it), a single host call per write for atomicity, and the 16 MiB / 8 MiB ceilings as real constants. Four sub-claims are contradicted by primary sources. (1) NativeImage is not immutable: setTemplateImage, addRepresentation and the writable isMacTemplateImage property mutate it. (2) createFromPath is not 'one FsBroker fs.read': it returns synchronously and, for a name without a DPI suffix, reads the base file plus eleven suffixed siblings (@2x, @3x, @1x, @4x, ...), through an asar-aware reader. (3) createFromDataURL(png).toPNG() is not a byte pass-through in Electron: the PNG is decoded into a Skia representation and toPNG re-encodes, so ancillary chunks are dropped and an invalid payload yields an empty image and an empty buffer. F06-T1's criterion 'toPNG() byte equality for PNG input' is therefore not a valid oracle in either direction. (4) The sync mechanism is misattributed and unavailable: Linear KEL-127 is the program issue 'post-audit convergence and Mac no-Rust product proof' and contains no blocking-CALL primitive; the 'blocking CALL with a deadline, rate-limited, dev-warned' rule is arch 02 text about renderer sendSync. The map's resolved fact is that the Bun kipc client cannot block, so 'Zettlr is runnable with a config-only change' is false until the worker-owned transport exists. The same gap covers NativeImage's synchronous transforms that Zettlr uses (resize, toJPEG(100), toDataURL, getAspectRatio), which D5 leaves host-side. Demand and sizing: Zettlr's resolved legacy clipboard demand is two call sites (one synchronous readText, one fire-and-forget writeImage); readImage, writeText and availableFormats have zero call sites, and Zettlr is the second corpus, so the quirk flag is not first-proof work. Also unevaluated: Bun 1.4.2 ships a built-in Bun.Image codec (system backend), which makes rejected alternative (b) 'pure-TS decode' a strawman - though it is Promise-only, so it does not by itself satisfy the sync contract.

decisions.question: How do dialog-chosen paths become filesystem authority for a strict-profile Bun main without a second policy owner or a widened manifest?
decisions.proposed_answer: Add one host-owned 'session grant' mint: the host dialog (AppProcess principal) returns paths AND registers each as a generation-bound fs scope (open → fs.read leaf; save → fs.write leaf) into the same FsBroker retained-scope set that KEL-130 built, revoked on Bun generation death and never persisted. Sibling policy is explicit: a dialog grant covers the chosen leaf plus a declared sibling pattern (`<name>.*` in the same directory) because the drawio oracle writes `.bkp`/draft siblings; anything wider requires a manifest grant. `keld migrate` seeds static dirs (arch 03 §3) but never seeds `$HOME/**`. Electron parity point: apps see identical return shapes; the difference is that out-of-grant fs calls from the node:fs facade fail with KELD-GUARD002 instead of succeeding — recorded ✔ for the dialog cell and ▲ for the 'ambient fs after dialog' cell.

decisions.question: What is the object/identity model for host-owned UI handles (Menu, MenuItem, Tray, Notification, popup) across the Bun/host process boundary?
decisions.proposed_answer: Every F06 object is a host-main-thread resource with a host-assigned (generation, id) pair; the facade holds a proxy whose property setters are write-through kipc calls and whose events/clicks are host→Bun messages carrying (commandId, focusedWindowId, KeyboardEvent). Menu templates are submitted as one bounded tree per setApplicationMenu/popup (host builds, assigns commandIds, executes `role` items host-side without a round trip, exactly as Electron ignores `click` when `role` is set). The default menu is built host-side when the app never sets one. Lifetime: handles die with their Bun generation (tray icons, popups, notifications, power assertions are released) — a deliberate ▲ versus Electron's GC-driven Tray lifetime. Accelerator normalization is one host-side parser shared by menu and globalShortcut.
